findings.quoted_text: Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, without notice and without further payment.
All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.

The parties acknowledge that the description of the Services is intended to identify the principal workstreams. Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
A Deliverable is accepted when Client provides written acceptance or when the review period expires without a written rejection describing a material nonconformity.
Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, without notice and without further payment.
findings.explanation: The client can end the relationship whenever they want and stop paying you, even if you have already performed work or incurred costs. This leaves you uncompensated for effort already expended.
findings.suggested_change: Add a clause requiring the client to provide at least 15 days written notice and to pay all undisputed fees for services rendered up to the termination date, plus any reasonable wind‑down costs.

findings.quoted_text: All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.
findings.explanation: Ownership of your work shifts to the client before you have been paid for it. If the client delays or refuses payment, you have already lost control of the IP you created.
findings.suggested_change: Tie the IP transfer to full payment: "All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon receipt of payment for that Deliverable."

findings.quoted_text: The parties acknowledge that the description of the Services is intended to identify the principal workstreams. Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
findings.explanation: The wording allows the client to request minor changes without a formal change order, which could gradually expand the scope and increase your workload without additional compensation.
findings.suggested_change: Specify that any clarification that could affect effort or cost must be documented as a change request and approved in writing before work proceeds.

findings.quoted_text: A Deliverable is accepted when Client provides written acceptance or when the review period expires without a written rejection describing a material nonconformity.
findings.explanation: If the client simply does not respond within 10 days, the Deliverable is deemed accepted, potentially triggering payment while the client may still have concerns or want changes.
findings.suggested_change: Require explicit written acceptance for each Deliverable; if the client does not respond within the review period, the parties must discuss and mutually agree on acceptance rather than an automatic deeming.

findings.quoted_text: Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.explanation: A 30‑day payment window is standard, but the monthly interest of 1% (≈12% annual) can become costly if the client delays payment repeatedly.
findings.suggested_change: Cap interest at a reasonable annual rate (e.g., 12% per annum) or require interest only after a 60‑day grace period, and include a right to suspend services after 45 days of non‑payment.

findings.explanation: The contract only allows three rounds of revisions. If the Client requests additional changes after the three rounds, they may still expect the work to be done without extra compensation, which could force you to perform extra work beyond the agreed scope.
findings.suggested_change: Specify that any revisions beyond the three allotted rounds will be treated as a change request and billed at an agreed hourly rate or require a written amendment and additional fee.

findings.explanation: Payments are due 30 days after invoicing, and the interest on late payments is only 1.0% per annum, which may not adequately compensate you for cash‑flow delays or the cost of financing the work.
findings.suggested_change: Negotiate a shorter payment term (e.g., Net 15) and a higher late‑payment interest rate (e.g., 1.5% per month or 18% per annum), or increase the initial deposit percentage to improve cash flow.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body:
Hi,

I have reviewed the agreement and would like to suggest a few adjustments before signing:

- The agreement currently allows termination without notice or further payment. I propose requiring at least 15 days written notice and payment of all undisputed fees up to the termination date, plus reasonable wind‑down costs.
- The relevant clause transfers all intellectual property rights to the client upon delivery. I suggest tying the transfer to full payment for each deliverable.
- The description of services permits minor clarifications without a formal change order. I recommend that any clarification that could affect effort or cost be documented as a change request and approved in writing before work proceeds.
- Acceptance of a deliverable is deemed automatic if the client does not respond within the review period. I propose requiring explicit written acceptance; if no response is received, the parties should discuss and mutually agree on acceptance.
- The revision allowance is limited to three rounds. I propose that any revisions beyond the three rounds be treated as a change request and billed at an agreed hourly rate or require a written amendment and additional fee.

Thank you for considering these changes. I look forward to finalizing the agreement.

Best regards
